   NCFFA Agenda Report
  October 21, 2025

TO:  Honorable Norwalk Facilities Financing Authority Commission

FROM:  Jesus M. Gomez, Chief Administrative Officer

BY:  Alex Hamilton, Interim Director of Community Development
  Sandra Duran, Senior Management Analyst

SUBJECT: RESOLUTION NO. NCFFA-24 - APPROVING AN AMENDED AND RESTATED
  PARKING AGREEMENT

Background:

The County of Los Angeles (“County”) and City are parties to a Ground Lease Agreement dated
March 30, 1995 (the “Parking Ground Lease”), pursuant to which the County leases to certain
real property in the City, in turn the County leased the Parking Structure Parcel to City in order
to facilitate the development and operation of the Parking Structure for use by the City and the
County. On April 1, 1995, a Site Sublease entered by the City, as sublessor, and Norwalk
Community Facilities Financing Authority (“NCFFA”), as sublessee. The NCFFA developed the
Parking Structure Parcel with a multi-level parking structure (the “Parking Structure”) containing
approximately 1,010 vehicle parking spaces, and a pedestrian bridge (the “Pedestrian Bridge”).
A Lease Agreement dated April 1, 1995 (the “City Leaseback Agreement”), entered by and
between the NCFFA, as lessor, and the City, as lessee, the NCFFA leased the Parking Structure
and Pedestrian Bridge back to the City and the City continues to operate the Parking Structure.

The City, NCFFA, Theater Developer, and AMC are parties to a Parking Agreement dated
May 15, 1995, a copy of which was recorded on June 14, 1995 as Instrument No. 95-948752
(the “1995 Agreement”) in the Official Records, as amended by that certain Amendment to
Parking Agreement dated May 15, 1995, a copy of which was recorded on June 14, 1995 as
Instrument No. 95-948753 in the Official Records (the “First Amendment”). A Second
Amendment to Parking Agreement dated June 12, 1997, a copy of which was recorded on
June 19, 1997 as Instrument No. 97-917901 in the Official Records (the “Second Amendment”)
and together with the 1995 Agreement and the First Amendment, the (“Original Parking
Agreement”), regarding the Parking Structure.
 NCFFA  October 21, 2025
Resolution No. NCFFA-24  Page No. 2

In the Original Parking Agreement, the City granted to the Theater Developer and AMC, and
upon any termination of the Theater Ground Lease and/or Theater Lease, to the operator of the
Theater Complex covering the Theater Parcel (a “Theater Operator”) and together with Theater
Developer and AMC certain non-exclusive rights to utilize vehicle parking spaces in the Parking
Structure and in the City Hall surface parking area (“Surface Parking Area”). The Ground Lease
dated December 19, 2022, as amended by that certain First Amendment to Ground Lease dated
March 31, 2025 (as amended, the “Project Ground Lease”), entered into by and between the
City and Primestor; the City leased a portion of City Property, including but not limited to the
Surface Parking Area to Primestor for the development and construction of a mixed use
development (the “Mixed-Use Project”) consisting of (i) approximately three hundred seventy-
four (374) residential units; (ii) approximately 94,398 square feet of commercial uses, which may
include, but not be limited to, food and beverage establishments, retail, health and wellness
facilities, and grocery or supermarket uses; and (iii) approximately 119,643 square feet of
ground-floor open space/plaza area that is publicly accessible but privately maintained and
operated.

The City, NCFFA, Theater Developer, and AMC desire to amend and restate the Original Parking
Agreement, in its entirety, in order to permit patrons, customers, and employees (herein
collectively called “Permittees”) of each of Theater Parties, Primestor Parties, and each party or
parties in possession, which shall include tenants, subtenants, concessionaires and licensees,
from time to time, of the Theater Complex and the Mixed-Use Project.

Analysis:

These amendments will clarify the operational characteristics of the Civic Center garage for all
parties. With the completion of the Walk project and ongoing successful operations of the AMC
theater, along with the County and State operations, it’s anticipated there will be a change in the
manner in which parking in the garage is used. Briefly, the Amended and Restated Parking
Agreement does the following:

  a. Primestor’s Rights to Take Over Operation and Maintenance of Parking Structure
  (Section 4.2(b)) – Primestor will have the right to take over parking structure operations
  and maintenance (“O&M”). Costs of O&M currently are borne by the City. If Primestor
  elects to take over O&M, the costs would be determined under a management agreement
  between City and Primestor to be negotiated and entered into later. The City would
  continue to receive parking revenue.
  b. Theater Parking Study and Potential for Exclusive Theater Parking (Section 4.3(a)) – The
  City and Primestor agreed that language authorizing the movie theater up to 500
  exclusive parking spaces needed to remain. Therefore, the parking agreement was
  revised as follows:
  i. Allows a maximum of 500 exclusive theater parking spaces during hours of operation.
  ii. The number of exclusive theater parking spaces would be limited to the number of
  parking spaces justified in the parking study but not exceed 500 parking spaces. It is
  important to note that while 500 spaces are dedicated for the AMC theater, previous
  parking studies have shown that even during peak demand periods that number is
  never close to being exceeded. In the event, that during future operation of the garage
  it appears that number is close to being approached, AMC would have to justify the
 NCFFA  October 21, 2025
Resolution No. NCFFA-24  Page No. 3

  need for the full 500 spaces with a parking study subject to review and consideration
  by all parties to the agreement.
  iii. Exclusive theater parking spaces would be “paused” if the theater complex ceases
  operation for 90 day consecutive days and resume once operations restart.
  iv. If exclusive theater parking is triggered, the City is to be allocated 250 non-exclusive
  parking spaces between the hours of 6:30 a.m. and 6:30 p.m. on Mondays,
  Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays, and between the hours of 6:30 a.m. and
  5:00 p.m. on Fridays under the parking plan. This addresses the City’s concern that
  adequate parking remain in the garage for City Hall patrons, City Staff, fleet vehicles,
  and Public Safety.

Environmental Review:

The City Council hereby finds that the Amended and Restated Parking Agreement is
categorically exempt pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (“CEQA”) as this
activity will not have a significant effect on the environment per Section 15301 Class 1 (Existing
Facilities) of the CEQA Guidelines and CEQA Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3) – Common Sense
Exemption in that it can be seen with certainty that there is no possibility that the Amended and
Restated Parking Agreement may have a significant effect on the environment. None of the
exceptions under CEQA Guidelines Section 15300.2 apply.

Fiscal Impact:

N/A

Citizens Advised:

N/A

Strategic Plan 2023 Implementation:

The recommended action will further the City’s Strategic Plan Goal 3: Build Great Public
Destinations and would contribute implementation of the Specific Plan.

Recommended Action:

Staff recommends the Authority adopt Resolution No. NCFFA-24, A RESOLUTION OF THE
NORWALK COMMUNITY FACILITIES FINANCING AUTHORITY APPROVING AN AMENDED
AND RESTATED PARKING AGREEMENT.

NOW THEREFORE, THE NORWALK COMMUNITY FACILITIES FINANCING AUTHORITY
RESOLVES:

  Section 1. The foregoing recitals are true and correct and are hereby incorporated
as substantive findings in this Resolution.

  Section 2. The Authority hereby finds that the Amended and Restated Parking
Agreement is categorically exempt pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act
(“CEQA”) as this activity will not have a significant effect on the environment per Section
15301 Class 1 (Existing Facilities) of the CEQA Guidelines and CEQA Guidelines Section
15061(b)(3) – Common Sense Exemption in that it can be seen with certainty that there is no
possibility that the Amended and Restated Parking Agreement may have a significant effect
on the environment. None of the exceptions under CEQA Guidelines Section 15300.2 apply.

  Section 3. The Authority hereby approves the Amended and Restated Parking
Agreement. The Authority Director or his designee are hereby authorized and directed to
execute Amended and Restated Parking Agreement along with any and all revisions,
insertions, and omissions therein as may be required consistent with the intent of this
Resolution and approved by the Authority Counsel.

  Section 4. The Authority further authorizes the Authority Director or designee to
prepare, execute, or record (or cause to be recorded) any and all ancillary documents,
instruments, certificates, or amendments, in a form approved by the Authority Counsel,
related to the Amended and Restated Parking Agreement, provided that such documents or
amendments do not materially modify the essential terms or financial obligations of the City
provided there is funding in the budget, and that are consistent with the intent of this
Resolution.
